The asymmetry is independent of the LDME at leading order for $J/ψ$-photon production. Thus, the Sivers asymmetry in both processes is a robust probe of the gluon Sivers function.

AI.tldr: The paper estimates the Sivers asymmetry in back-to-back $J/ψ$-photon and $J/ψ$-jet production at the Electron-Ion Collider, using a TMD factorization framework and NRQCD model, highlighting the robustness of the asymmetry as a probe of the gluon Sivers function.
AI.motivation: To investigate the Sivers asymmetry in specific processes to gain insights into the gluon Sivers function, which is less understood.
AI.method: Utilizing a transverse momentum dependent factorization framework and NRQCD model to analyze $J/ψ$ production mechanisms, incorporating TMD evolution in the calculations.
AI.result: The gluon induced channel predominates, resulting in a sizeable Sivers asymmetry in both $J/ψ$-photon and $J/ψ$-jet production, remaining robust against variations in the long-distance matrix element.
AI.conclusion: The observed Sivers asymmetry serves as a reliable and significant probe of the gluon Sivers function, with implications for experimental studies at the EIC.

title: Qubit Readout via State-Dependent Radiative Linewidths
summary: Fast qubit readout conventionally encodes state information in a dispersive frequency shift. Here we formulate a linewidth-encoded quantum non-demolition measurement channel in which the qubit state enters the external radiative amplitude, equivalently a state-dependent Lindblad jump operator. Starting from an empty cavity, we show analytically that this dissipative channel imprints state information on the output field at $O(t)$, whereas standard dispersive readout starts at $O(t^2)$ because it requires intracavity buildup and conditional phase accumulation. This short-time scaling produces faster matched-filter signal-to-noise ratio accumulation and persists in finite-resource comparisons, including photon-number limits, external-linewidth budgets, cavity depletion, and pulse-optimized dispersive baselines. We further outline an auxiliary-mode route that converts a qubit-state-dependent auxiliary susceptibility into a state-dependent linewidth. These results identify engineered dissipation as an information-carrying resource for fast quantum non-demolition readout.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a linewidth-encoded quantum non-demolition measurement channel that enables faster qubit readout than conventional methods by utilizing dissipative channels that imprint state information on the output field more rapidly.
AI.motivation: To develop a faster qubit readout method that surpasses the limitations of conventional dispersive frequency shift techniques, which rely on intracavity buildup and longer timescales for signal accumulation.
AI.method: The authors formulate a linewidth-encoded measurement channel where qubit states influence the external radiative amplitude, thereby employing a state-dependent Lindblad jump operator that provides a faster imprinting of state information on the output field.
AI.result: The dissipative channel achieves state information transfer at $O(t)$, leading to faster signal-to-noise ratio gains compared to the traditional $O(t^2)$ dispersive readout method, even under resource limitations.
AI.conclusion: Engineered dissipation serves as a valuable resource for fast quantum non-demolition readout, highlighting its potential in improving qubit state measurements through novel channel dynamics.

title: Unveiling Radio Transients with SKAO Telescopes
comment: Published in Advancing Astrophysics with the SKA II (AASKAII), 2026 (arXiv:2606.20366). Report-no:AASKAII/Miller-Jones01. Advancing Astrophysics with the SKA II (AASKAII) outlines the transformative scientific advances that will be enabled by the SKA telescopes
summary: Transient astrophysics provides a set of unique laboratories for studying fundamental physics. From the launching of powerful relativistic jets to merging neutron stars, highly-magnetised compact objects, or stellar explosions, transients probe the Universe at its most extreme. The SKAO will provide an unrivalled set of capabilities for transient observations on timescales from nanoseconds to decades, opening new discovery space. With its sensitivity, broad spectral coverage, wide field of view, and high survey speed, SKAO will allow us to discover and understand rare events that provide powerful new insights into regimes of high energy density, strong gravity, and intense magnetic fields. Complemented by a suite of multi-wavelength and multi-messenger facilities, and supported by a network of smaller existing radio telescopes and new computational capabilities, SKAO will unveil the most powerful and exotic events in our Universe, addressing some of the key questions in modern astrophysics and cosmology.

AI.tldr: The SKAO will transform transient astrophysics by enabling unprecedented observations of extreme cosmic events, enhancing our understanding of fundamental physics.
AI.motivation: Understanding extreme phenomena in the universe, such as relativistic jets and neutron star mergers, is crucial for fundamental physics.
AI.method: Using SKAO's advanced capabilities in terms of sensitivity, spectral coverage, field of view, and speed for transient observations across various timescales, complemented by multi-wavelength and multi-messenger approaches.
AI.result: SKAO is expected to discover rare cosmic events and enhance insights into high-energy density, strong gravity, and intense magnetic fields.
AI.conclusion: SKAO will provide significant contributions to addressing fundamental questions in astrophysics and cosmology through its unique observational capabilities.

title: Design and Performance of the Carruthers Geocoronal Imager
comment: Preprint, in review by Space Sciences Reviews. To be published as part of the Carruthers mission special issue
summary: The GeoCoronal Imager (GCI) onboard the Carruthers Geocorona Observatory is the primary scientific instrument of the mission. It is designed to measure far ultraviolet light at 121.6 nm (Lyman-alpha) emitted by hydrogen (H) atoms in Earth's exosphere with the sensitivity, accuracy and precision to meet the mission's scientific objectives regarding the nature of terrestrial exospheric structure and dynamics on both global and regional scales. The GCI is comprised of two co-aligned UV imaging systems. The Narrow Field Imager (NFI) acquires nearly continuous images of exospheric Lyman-alpha radiance near and above the Earth's limb at relatively high spatial and temporal resolution, while the Wide Field Imager (WFI) uses relatively higher optical sensitivity and a wider field of view to detect faint Lyman-alpha emission from the exosphere's outermost extent. Both imaging channels feature identical active pixel sensor cameras, gain-intensifiers, and 6-position optical filter wheels. This paper outlines the instrument design requirements, informed by mission science goals, as well as its performance as measured in the vacuum ultraviolet laboratory test and calibration.

AI.tldr: The GeoCoronal Imager (GCI) measures far ultraviolet light emitted by hydrogen in Earth's exosphere, featuring two co-aligned imaging systems for high-resolution and wide-field imaging to fulfill scientific objectives.
AI.motivation: The mission aims to enhance understanding of the structure and dynamics of Earth's exosphere on global and regional scales through precise measurement of exospheric Lyman-alpha radiance.
AI.method: The GCI includes two co-aligned imaging systems: the Narrow Field Imager (NFI) for high-resolution imaging and the Wide Field Imager (WFI) for detecting faint emissions, both utilizing active pixel sensors and optical filter wheels.
AI.result: Instrument performance was evaluated through vacuum ultraviolet laboratory tests and calibration, meeting design requirements based on scientific goals.
AI.conclusion: The GCI is equipped to meet the scientific objectives of understanding the terrestrial exosphere effectively through its innovative dual-imaging approach.

title: Evidence for differential kinetic freeze-out of the $φ(1020)$ meson in Pb-Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}} = 2.76$ TeV
summary: In heavy-ion collisions, hadronic species with small interaction cross sections may decouple from the evolving fireball earlier than the bulk, yet quantitative evidence for this differential freeze-out has remained elusive. We report that the $φ(1020)$ meson does \emph{not} kinetically freeze out with the bulk hadrons in 0--5\% central Pb-Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}} = 2.76$ TeV: a Boltzmann-Gibbs blast-wave contour analysis of ALICE $φ(1020)$ $p_{\rm T}$ transverse-momentum spectra shows that the bulk $π/K/p$ freeze-out point is excluded at $4.1σ$ ($Δχ^2 = 21.7$). Despite its proton-like mass, the $φ$ exhibits freeze-out parameters incompatible with those of the bulk hadrons, implying that the observed spectral hardening cannot be attributed solely to mass-dependent collective expansion. Instead, it is naturally explained by the OZI-suppressed $φ$-hadron interaction cross section which causes $φ$ to decouple earlier and probe a distinct freeze-out surface. The exclusion is robust under all systematic variations tested and is qualitatively reproduced by SMASH hadronic transport simulations. These findings establish the $φ$ meson as a clean probe of species-dependent hadronization, and provide quantitative evidence for a kinetic freeze-out hierarchy in ultra-relativistic heavy-ion collisions.

AI.tldr: The study shows that the $φ(1020)$ meson kinetically decouples earlier than bulk hadrons in heavy-ion collisions, evidenced by a significant exclusion from the bulk freeze-out parameters.
AI.motivation: To provide quantitative evidence of differential freeze-out for hadronic species in heavy-ion collisions, particularly focusing on the $φ(1020)$ meson.
AI.method: A Boltzmann-Gibbs blast-wave contour analysis of ALICE transverse-momentum spectra for $φ(1020)$ mesons was conducted, comparing freeze-out parameters with bulk hadrons ($	ext{π, K, p}$).
AI.result: The $φ(1020)$ meson demonstrates a freeze-out point excluded from that of bulk hadrons at a significance of $4.1σ$, indicating distinct decoupling behavior associated with its small interaction cross section.
AI.conclusion: The findings establish the $φ$ meson as an effective probe for investigating hadronization dynamics, illustrating a kinetic freeze-out hierarchy in the context of ultra-relativistic heavy-ion collisions.

title: Spin-Squeezing-Enhanced Charging for Quantum Dicke Batteries
summary: High-power Dicke quantum batteries (QBs) typically exploit collective superradiance, whereas intrinsic matter-matter interactions are conventionally considered detrimental. Here, we propose a counterintuitive paradigm: these interactions can be controlled and repurposed as a synergistic resource to enhance charging power and capacity. In the low-excitation limit, transverse interactions induce collective spin squeezing, causing critical mode softening and an exponential enhancement of effective coupling, which significantly boosts charging power. At higher excitations, these interactions act as a macroscopic nonlinear torque. By appropriately aligning this torque, we effectively lower phase-space dynamical barriers, guiding the system along optimal rapid-charging paths. Importantly, this cooperative enhancement remains highly robust under realistic dissipation, outperforming ideal, dissipationless Dicke QBs in specific regimes. Our results provide a blueprint for exploiting matter interactions to design dissipation-resistant, high-performance many-body QBs.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces a method to enhance high-power Dicke quantum batteries by repurposing matter-matter interactions, resulting in improved charging performance and robustness against dissipation.
AI.motivation: To explore the potential benefits of intrinsic matter-matter interactions in enhancing the performance of Dicke quantum batteries, typically seen as detrimental.
AI.method: The authors develop a framework that utilizes transverse interactions for collective spin squeezing and nonlinear torque to lower dynamical barriers and facilitate rapid charging.
AI.result: The proposed framework significantly enhances the charging power and capacity of quantum batteries, surpassing traditional Dicke QBs under certain conditions, even with realistic dissipation present.
AI.conclusion: The findings suggest a novel approach to designing high-performance, dissipation-resistant many-body quantum batteries by leveraging controlled interactions.

title: The location of the upper edge of the pair-instability supernovae black hole mass gap
summary: Gravitational wave observations are beginning to probe the upper edge of the pair-instability supernova (PISN) black hole mass gap, a key prediction of stellar evolution. In this work, we quantify the sensitivity of this boundary to uncertainties in stellar evolution using a suite of simulations that vary inputs including nuclear reaction rates, mixing processes, and stellar winds. We find that the $^{12}{\rm C}(α,γ)^{16}{\rm O}$ reaction rate is the dominant source of uncertainty, shifting the upper edge by $ΔM\sim30\,{\rm M}_\odot$, with the triple-$α$ rate producing a comparable shift of $\sim25\,{\rm M}_\odot$. Notably, $^{16}{\rm O}+^{16}{\rm O}$ reactions shift the upper edge by $\sim15\,{\rm M}_\odot$ while leaving the lower edge unchanged, implying they can widen or narrow the mass gap. Other processes affect the location at the $\lesssim10\,{\rm M}_\odot$ level. In contrast to the lower edge, we find that the upper edge is robust to variations in spatial and temporal resolution, indicating that it is reliably resolved in current simulations. Our results demonstrate that the upper edge carries substantial theoretical uncertainty and, while comparatively less affected by astrophysical contamination than the lower edge, provides a direct probe of the nuclear processes governing pair instability. We discuss the implications for interpreting high-mass black hole detections in gravitational wave data.

AI.tldr: Gravitational wave data reveals uncertainties in black hole mass gaps, particularly at the upper edge influenced by nuclear reaction rates.
AI.motivation: To explore how uncertainties in stellar evolution influence the boundaries of the pair-instability supernova black hole mass gap.
AI.method: Simulations varying nuclear reaction rates, mixing processes, and stellar winds were employed to assess their impacts on black hole mass limits.
AI.result: Key reactions were identified: the $^{12}{m C}(α,γ)^{16}{m O}$ rate shifted the upper edge by $ΔM	ext{∼}30	ext{M}_	ext{☉}$, while the triple-$α$ rate shifted it by $	ext{∼}25	ext{M}_	ext{☉}$; other reactions caused smaller shifts.
AI.conclusion: The upper edge of the mass gap shows substantial theoretical uncertainty but is less affected by external astrophysical factors, serving as a direct indicator of nuclear processes related to pair instability.

title: Early Telescope Throughput Results from the Collimated Beam Projector at the Vera C. Rubin Observatory
summary: The Vera C. Rubin Observatory LSST requires precise photometric calibration to meet its science goals, particularly for cosmological analyses based on Type Ia supernovae. The Collimated Beam Projector (CBP) has been developed to support this effort by projecting monochromatic point sources of known wavelength and flux directly into the telescope aperture, enabling direct in situ measurements of the full system throughput. We present initial results demonstrating the CBP capability to characterize the instrumental response of the Rubin Telescope and to measure the transmission profiles of LSSTCam broadband filters. In particular, the CBP enables spatially resolved mapping of filter bandpass edge shifts across the focal plane, which can vary by several nanometers as a function of the ray angle of incidence. These early results establish the CBP as a powerful photometric calibration tool and lay the groundwork for continuous throughput monitoring throughout LSST operations.

AI.tldr: The CBP aids the LSST in precise photometric calibration for cosmological analyses by projecting monochromatic sources into the telescope, enabling thorough characterization of its response and filter transmissions.
AI.motivation: To achieve accurate measurements necessary for cosmological analyses, particularly involving Type Ia supernovae.
AI.method: The Collimated Beam Projector (CBP) projects known wavelength and flux monochromatic point sources directly into the telescope's aperture for direct throughput measurements.
AI.result: Initial results show the CBP's effectiveness in characterizing the Rubin Telescope's response and measuring transmission profiles of LSSTCam filters, highlighting variations in bandpass edge shifts due to the angle of incidence.
AI.conclusion: The CBP is established as a vital tool for photometric calibration and will support ongoing throughput monitoring during LSST operations.

title: EasyScan_HEP 2: Agent-Ready Parameter Scans for High-Energy Physics
summary: AI agents are beginning to reshape the preparation and steering of computational workflows in high-energy physics phenomenology. To accommodate this change, we upgrade EasyScan_HEP to make the construction of parameter-scan configuration files more accessible to AI assistance. EasyScan_HEP 2 exposes agent-facing command-line and machine-readable interfaces, allowing an assistant to translate natural language requests into an explicit .ini configuration that defines the scan method, external-program workflow, constraints, and outputs. The resulting configuration can be inspected through a local Web UI. The framework also supports AI-assisted extension to new scan methods, as illustrated by the integration of BESTFIT, EMCEE, and DYNESTY. In this way, EasyScan_HEP 2 adapts parameter scans to AI-assisted workflows while preserving reproducibility, transparency, and user control.

AI.tldr: EasyScan_HEP 2 upgrades parameter-scan configuration for AI assistance in high-energy physics, allowing natural language requests to create executable configurations while maintaining reproducibility and user control.
AI.motivation: To facilitate AI integration in computational workflows within high-energy physics phenomenology, enhancing accessibility and usability.
AI.method: Upgraded EasyScan_HEP exposes command-line and machine-readable interfaces, enabling translation of natural language requests into .ini configuration files that define scan methods and workflows.
AI.result: The framework supports AI-assisted extensions and integrates scanning methods like BESTFIT, EMCEE, and DYNESTY, streamlining the parameter scan process.
AI.conclusion: EasyScan_HEP 2 enables AI-assisted workflows in parameter scans while ensuring reproducibility and user control.

title: Continuous-Variable Source-Independent Quantum Random Number Generation with General POVMs
summary: Continuous-variable source-independent quantum random number generators offer the highest generation rates among semi-device-independent protocols. In reality, the protocol design is limited due to permissible measurement configurations. In this work, we propose a rigorous security proof framework that accommodates general, infinite-dimensional positive-operator-valued measures. Building upon the numerical security proof framework, we evaluate the randomness lower bound by maximizing the eavesdropper's guessing probability. Specifically, we transform the inherently infinite-dimensional semidefinite program in Fock space into a tractable finite-dimensional one, rigorously proving that latter provides a strict upper bound to the guessing probability of the original infinite-dimensional problem. Our framework showcases its capability by certifying secure randomness using unbalanced homodyne detection with only a single quadrature measurement, thereby bypassing the traditional requirement of measuring two conjugate quadratures such as $X$ and $P$. We experimentally validate our protocol on an optical platform using vacuum and weak coherent states, achieving a maximum secure randomness extraction of 1.11 bits per sample and an ultra-high generation rate of 1.776 Gbps. This work provides a flexible design for practical, high-speed quantum random number generators.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a security proof framework for continuous-variable quantum random number generators that enhances randomness extraction capabilities using innovative measurement strategies. It achieves high generation rates and experimental validation.
AI.motivation: To improve the design and security of continuous-variable quantum random number generators, enabling higher generation rates and less restrictive measurement configurations.
AI.method: A rigorous security proof framework is developed that accommodates infinite-dimensional positive-operator-valued measures, transforming complex infinite-dimensional programs into tractable finite versions while maximizing eavesdropper's guessing probability.
AI.result: The proposed method allows for secure randomness generation with unbalanced homodyne detection, achieving 1.11 bits per sample and 1.776 Gbps in an optical platform experiment with vacuum and weak coherent states.
AI.conclusion: This work demonstrates a flexible design for practical, high-speed quantum random number generators, improving the efficiency and security of random number extraction.

title: Evidence for Millihertz Oscillations in the bright atoll source GX 3+1
summary: We report evidence for millihertz (mHz) QPOs in the bright atoll neutron star low-mass X-ray binary (NS LMXB) source GX 3+1 using NICER in the 0.5--10 keV energy band. Across 7 observational datasets obtained over 6 days, we made 8 candidate mHz QPO detections with local significance above 95%, one of which remains above 95% global significance after the trial correction. These mHz QPOs were detected in the 7--15 mHz frequency range and had fractional rms amplitudes ranging from 0.51--1.41%. Our studies indicate no association between the hardness intensity diagram location of the candidate QPOs and their rms amplitudes. There appears to be a monotonous increase in rms with energy, except in some observations where there is a pivot around 3--4 keV or at ~ 5 keV. Previous studies of mHz QPOs in other sources in literature indicate a pivot around 3 keV in the rms-energy relation, but in our study some tentative detections suggest a pivot at around ~ 5 keV, though the large uncertainties in most cases prevent a robust statistical claim. Although properties such as the frequency range of detection and fractional rms amplitudes of the mHz QPOs in our study are well in agreement with that in literature for other NS LMXBs, the luminosity at which these candidate QPOs occur are higher than that of other sources. The rms-energy relation of the candidate mHz QPOs and the luminosity at which they occur challenges some of the existing considerations of mHz QPO origin.

AI.tldr: This study reports the detection of millihertz QPOs in the neutron star binary GX 3+1, revealing unique characteristics in their rms-energy relation and luminosity.
AI.motivation: To investigate millihertz QPOs in the neutron star binary GX 3+1 and compare the findings with existing literature.
AI.method: Utilized NICER to analyze observational datasets, detecting QPOs in the 0.5-10 keV band and assessing their statistical significance and properties.
AI.result: Detected 8 candidate mHz QPOs in the 7–15 mHz range, exhibiting fractional rms amplitudes of 0.51–1.41%. Observed unique rms-energy relations with potential pivot points around 3-4 keV and ~5 keV.
AI.conclusion: The study finds that the properties of the detected QPOs suggest higher luminosity levels and challenge existing models on mHz QPO origins.

title: In Situ Measurements of the Reflectances of the LSSTCam Optics and Assessing the Impact of Optical Ghosts
summary: Optical ghosts are image artifacts caused by successive reflections of light between optical surfaces such as lenses, filters, and detectors. These artifacts are unavoidable due to the nonzero reflectances of optical elements and are a major source of contamination for low-surface-brightness science. We use optical ray tracing simulations tuned to observations from LSST Commissioning to quantify the impact of optical ghosts on the LSST data. In particular, we find that ~0.57% of the LSSTCam focal plane is impacted by optical ghosts when averaged across all bands. We also use data from the Collimated Beam Projector to measure the reflectances of various optical elements, generally confirming estimates of ~2% from the systems engineering throughput predictions.

AI.tldr: The study quantifies the impact of optical ghosts on LSST data, finding ~0.57% of the focal plane affected, and confirms reflectance estimates of ~2% from other predictions.
AI.motivation: To understand and quantify the contamination caused by optical ghosts in low-surface-brightness science, as they are a significant issue in imaging systems.
AI.method: Optical ray tracing simulations were performed alongside measurements from the Collimated Beam Projector to assess the influence of optical ghosts and to measure reflectances of optical elements.
AI.result: Approximately 0.57% of the LSSTCam focal plane is affected by optical ghosts on average across all bands, confirming an estimated reflectance of ~2% for optical elements.
AI.conclusion: The findings highlight a quantifiable level of optical ghost contamination that must be considered in low-surface-brightness scientific analyses.

title: Boosted Higgs-strahlung off a $W$ boson at next-to-next-to-next-to-leading order in QCD
summary: The production of a boosted Higgs boson in association with a charged weak ($W$) boson is a key process to scrutinize the electroweak symmetry breaking mechanism at hadron colliders. This reaction constitutes the dominant Higgs production channel at large transverse momentum, providing unique sensitivity to Higgs-boson interactions with other Standard Model particles as well as to physics beyond the Standard Model. In this Letter, we present the first fully differential calculation of this important scattering process at next-to-next-to-next-to-leading order (N$^3$LO) in perturbative Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD). We find that the N$^3$LO corrections, amounting to approximately $+2\%$ in the boosted regime, generally lie at the edge of or outside the standard scale variation band of the previous perturbative order. The residual dependence of the N$^3$LO prediction on perturbative scales is reduced to below the percent level, marking a milestone for the Higgs precision program.

AI.tldr: First fully differential calculation of boosted Higgs boson production with a charged weak boson at N$^3$LO in QCD shows significant corrections and reduced scale dependence.
AI.motivation: To scrutinize the electroweak symmetry breaking mechanism through Higgs production at hadron colliders, focusing on the dominant channel at large transverse momentum.
AI.method: Presentation of a fully differential calculation of boosted Higgs boson production at next-to-next-to-next-to-leading order (N$^3$LO) in QCD.
AI.result: N$^3$LO corrections yield approximately +2% in the boosted regime, with results lying outside previous perturbative scale variation bands.
AI.conclusion: The N$^3$LO prediction exhibits reduced scale dependence, achieving below one percent, which is a notable advancement for the Higgs precision program.

title: Generalised quantum interference
summary: Hong-Ou-Mandel interference is one of the clearest signatures of quantum behaviour: two identical photons meeting at a beam splitter always leave together. Here we demonstrate that this symmetry can be broken. Using a programmable integrated photonic processor, we interfere imbalanced two-photon states on a variable beam splitter and show that the output state of quantum interference can be continuously tuned, reaching the extreme case where destructive interference suppresses bunching at one output port. The asymmetry creates a forbidden bunching channel: photons may exit together at one port or separately at both ports, but cannot emerge together at the other port.

AI.tldr: The paper shows that Hong-Ou-Mandel interference can be altered using an integrated photonic processor to create an asymmetrical output from imbalanced two-photon states.
AI.motivation: To explore the limits of quantum behavior in photon interference and demonstrate that symmetry can be broken in specific conditions.
AI.method: Utilized a programmable integrated photonic processor to interfere imbalanced two-photon states on a variable beam splitter, allowing continuous tuning of the output state.
AI.result: Achieved a tunable output state where destructive interference can entirely suppress photon bunching at one output port, leading to a forbidden channel for photon exit.
AI.conclusion: The findings reveal a novel aspect of quantum interference that challenges conventional understanding and opens avenues for advanced quantum state manipulation.

title: High Frequency Wideband Study of FRB 20240114A with the Allen Telescope Array
comment: Submitted to AAS journals; comments are welcome
summary: We present a high-frequency, wideband observing campaign of the hyperactive repeating fast radio burst FRB 20240114A with the Allen Telescope Array. Between 27 January and 29 October 2024, we obtained 1167 hr of on-source observations across 1344 MHz of simultaneous bandwidth covering frequencies from approximately 900 MHz to 7620 MHz. We detected 97 bursts between ~900 MHz and ~5 GHz, including a strong S-band activity episode, while no bursts were detected in the highest-frequency tunings above ~5 GHz despite substantial exposure. This campaign provides one of the very few extended samples of repeating-FRB activity above 3 GHz, a regime that remains sparsely sampled. We find that the burst rate varies strongly with both observing frequency and epoch, confirming that the emission from FRB 20240114A is highly chromatic and band-limited. We measure the spectro-temporal properties of the bursts and their sub-components, confirming that fractional bandwidth remains approximately scale-invariant. Sub-burst durations decrease toward higher frequencies, and the magnitude of the downward drift rate increases with frequency. The cumulative spectral-energy-density distribution above our completeness threshold is well described by a shallow power law, indicating that high-energy bursts contribute substantially to the observed energy output. We also compare our detections with recently proposed long-timescale frequency-modulation models and find that the ATA high-frequency burst storm is not consistent with a strictly phase-coherent modulation inferred from other datasets. Our results demonstrate that incomplete time-frequency coverage can bias interpretations of burst activity and highlight the need for sustained, simultaneous wideband monitoring of hyperactive repeaters.

AI.tldr: A campaign observed fast radio burst FRB 20240114A, revealing high-frequency activity and strong variability in burst rates across frequencies.
AI.motivation: To investigate the chromatic and band-limited nature of FRB 20240114A and gather comprehensive data on its burst activity, particularly above 3 GHz.
AI.method: Utilized the Allen Telescope Array for 1167 hours of observations across a 1344 MHz bandwidth, monitoring frequencies from 900 MHz to 7620 MHz.
AI.result: Detected 97 bursts below 5 GHz, with no bursts above 5 GHz, showing high variability in burst rates and confirming the burst characteristics and energy distribution.
AI.conclusion: Findings stress the necessity for extensive, simultaneous observations to mitigate biases in understanding burst phenomena in hyperactive repeaters.

title: Determining stress-based bending mode limits for the Vera C. Rubin Observatory M1M3 active mirror system
comment: 9 pages, 3 figures, 3 tables, SPIE Astronomical Telescopes Instrumentation 2026
summary: The Vera C. Rubin Observatory Simonyi Survey Telescope's primary-tertiary mirror (M1M3) is an actively supported, 8.4-m cast borosilicate optic controlled by 156 pneumatic actuators. This work presents a rapid stress-estimation methodology based on the root-sum-square (RSS) combination of Finite Element Analysis to derive pre-computed unit bending mode stresses. Since the stress is proportional to strain, and strain is proportional to displacements, we theorized that since the bending mode displacements can be combined RSS, that the peak stresses would also combine by RSS. We validate the RSS-based major principal stress predictions against NASTRAN simulations for representative bending mode combinations, demonstrating agreement within a few percent for peak Principal major stress across the mirror glass substrate. Unit displacement and corresponding unit stress fields for the first 20 natural bending modes of the M1M3 system are generated using NASTRAN. Representative multi-mode corrections including combinations that include astigmatism, coma, and spherical modes of higher order are then analyzed to compare the resulting peak principal stresses with RSS-based predictions. The method enables near instantaneous evaluation of stress margins for active optics corrections, safety-limit checking, and actuator-force optimization during telescope operations. This paper outlines the formulation, implementation workflow, validation results, and practical use cases for integrating RSS-based stress prediction into the Vera C. Rubin Observatory's M1M3 active optics system.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a rapid stress-estimation methodology for the Vera C. Rubin Observatory's primary-tertiary mirror, utilizing an RSS approach validated against NASTRAN simulations.
AI.motivation: To improve the efficiency in evaluating stress margins for active optics corrections and actuator-force optimization in telescope operations.
AI.method: A root-sum-square (RSS) methodology combining Finite Element Analysis is used to derive pre-computed unit bending mode stresses and validate against NASTRAN simulations.
AI.result: Validation shows agreement within a few percent for peak principal stress predictions across the mirror substrate, with analysis of multi-mode corrections yielding stress comparisons.
AI.conclusion: The methodology enables quick assessments of stress in the M1M3 system, enhancing operational safety and optimization.

title: A B-factory continuum retune of PYTHIA 8 hadronization parameters using BELLE and BABAR identified-hadron data
summary: We refine the hadronization sector of a pp PYTHIA~8 tune in $e^+e^-\to q\bar q$ production using selected BELLE and BABAR measurements near the $Υ(4S)$ region. The study is performed with PYTHIA~8.316 and Rivet~4.1.1 and is restricted to parameters used in this $e^+e^-$ setup. Starting from the five-parameter hadronization subset of the pp tune, we carry out a staged extension guided by the remaining differences in the BELLE and BABAR data. The final comparison uses a fixed common set of 20,803 bins and samples of 1,000,000 generated events per analysis and tune point. On this basis, the selected refined tune gives a bin-weighted score of 73.42, compared with 76.49 for the Skands $e^+e^-$ reference and 79.22 for Monash~2013 $e^+e^-$. It remains the best-scoring tune for the BELLE charged-hadron, baryon, and single- and dihadron measurements, while Skands still performs better for the BABAR charged-hadron sample and the BELLE meson sample. The bin-weighted ordering is driven primarily by the BELLE 2020 sample. The refined tune gives a small but stable improvement for the selected BELLE and BABAR measurements, although clear differences between the individual datasets remain.

AI.tldr: The paper refines the hadronization sector of the PYTHIA~8 model using BELLE and BABAR data from $e^+e^-	o q ar q$ production, achieving a competitive bin-weighted score.
AI.motivation: To improve the hadronization modeling in the PYTHIA~8 framework based on empirical data from particle collisions.
AI.method: A staged extension of a five-parameter hadronization tune in PYTHIA~8, utilizing measurements from BELLE and BABAR with a large sample size for rigorous evaluation.
AI.result: The refined tune achieves a bin-weighted score of 73.42, slightly lower than Skands' 76.49 and Monash 2013's 79.22, but remains the best for specific BELLE measurements.
AI.conclusion: The refined model provides a stable improvement for BELLE and BABAR data, although disparities between datasets persist.

title: Quantum Derivative Pricing for SPDEs via BDSDE Representation
summary: We study quantum speedups of derivative pricing for stochastic partial differential equation (SPDE) models through their backward doubly stochastic differential equation (BDSDE) representations. We develop conditional and nested quantum-accelerated multilevel Monte Carlo (QA-MLMC) methods for estimating the resulting conditional and nested expectations, improving the sampling complexity of classical Monte Carlo methods from $\widetilde{O}(ε^{-2})$ to $\widetilde{O}(ε^{-1})$ within additive error $ε$. We apply the framework to derivative pricing and sensitivity analysis, providing quantum-accelerated estimators for prices as well as first-order and second-order Greeks, likelihood-ratio and Malliavin-weight representations for Greeks, and Heston-type stochastic-volatility models. To enable efficient multilevel coupling, we construct a family of Forward--Backward Taylor discretization schemes for the stochastic integrals arising in the BDSDE representations and establish global strong-error order one convergence for pricing and Greek estimators. Numerical experiments showcase our schemes for first-order and second-order Greeks can reach the required orders for the full quadratic quantum speedups.

AI.tldr: This paper explores quantum-enhanced methods for pricing derivatives in SPDE models using BDSDE representations, achieving significant sampling complexity improvements and demonstrating their application in derivative pricing and sensitivity analysis.
AI.motivation: The need for more efficient derivative pricing methods due to the limitations of classical Monte Carlo methods.
AI.method: Development of conditional and nested quantum-accelerated multilevel Monte Carlo (QA-MLMC) methods and Forward--Backward Taylor discretization schemes for stochastic integrals in BDSDE.
AI.result: Improvement of sampling complexity from $	ilde{O}(ε^{-2})$ to $	ilde{O}(ε^{-1})$ and demonstration of achieving quadratic quantum speedups in numerical experiments.
AI.conclusion: The proposed QA-MLMC methods offer significant enhancements in derivative pricing accuracy and efficiency, particularly for Greeks in Heston-type models.

title: A Suppressed Volumetric Rate of High-Luminosity Mid-Infrared Selected Tidal Disruption Events
comment: 11 pages, 4 figures (+ 4 pages, 4 figures in appendix); Accepted for publication in ApJ
summary: Tidal Disruption Events (TDEs) serve as direct probes of the population of supermassive black holes in the center of galaxies and are nowadays regularly detected in optical wide-field time-domain sky surveys. Recent studies have demonstrated that a large fraction of TDEs can be uniquely identified in the infrared (IR) waveband, but these studies have to date been limited to relatively nearby events. In this work, we searched for highly luminous IR-bright TDEs that are rare and thus missed by searches in the local universe. We performed a systematic search of the NEOWISE archive and developed a new selection criterion based on the evolution of the W1-W2 color to select TDE candidates. We identified 10 IR bright TDEs with peak luminosities above $L_{\rm peak\, W2} \simeq 3 \times 10^{43}$ erg s$^{-1}$ and estimated an event rate of $1.2^{+0.5}_{-0.4}\times10^{-10}$ Mpc$^{-3}$year$^{-1}$ for the luminosity range of our sample. Compared to the existing local luminosity function of lower luminosity events, we detect a suppressed rate for these highly luminous events. This turn-over in the luminosity function can be naturally explained by the suppressed amount of TDEs taking place in systems with larger black hole masses, thereby confirming the TDE nature of our sources.

AI.tldr: A systematic search for luminous IR-bright Tidal Disruption Events (TDEs) was conducted using the NEOWISE archive, identifying 10 candidates and estimating a suppressed event rate for highly luminous TDEs compared to lower luminosity counterparts.
AI.motivation: To explore and identify highly luminous Tidal Disruption Events (TDEs) that may be overlooked in local surveys, enhancing understanding of supermassive black hole populations in galaxies.
AI.method: A systematic search of the NEOWISE archive was performed using a new selection criterion based on the W1-W2 color evolution to identify potential TDE candidates.
AI.result: Identified 10 highly luminous IR-bright TDEs with peak luminosities above $L_{m peak W2} \simeq 3 \times 10^{43}$ erg s$^{-1}$ and an estimated event rate of $1.2^{+0.5}_{-0.4}\times10^{-10}$ Mpc$^{-3}$ year$^{-1}$, showing a suppressed detection rate for these luminous events when compared to lower luminosity events.
AI.conclusion: The findings suggest that the suppressed rate of highly luminous TDEs is due to a lower occurrence in systems with larger black hole masses, confirming the TDE nature of the identified sources.

title: Mechanical Studies of an Additional Light Baffle for the LSST Camera
summary: Commissioning the NSF-DOE Vera C. Rubin Observatory consisted of engineering operation and on-sky data-taking, initially with the Commissioning Camera followed by the commissioning run of the LSST Camera (LSSTCam). As with other wide-field astronomical projects, the Rubin team anticipated a significant amount of stray light effects which would necessitate investigation and systematic mitigation. This led the Rubin stray light working group to develop tools, including a robust model of the entire observatory in Zemax, to trace the light paths of stray light artifacts back to their sources. This model along with the other efforts of the working group enabled significant improvements in stray light mitigation leading up to the commencement of the Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST). One such potential source was identified as a small chamfer on the L3 lens, for which it was hypothesized that a simple baffle added inside of the LSSTCam near the L3 should prove beneficial to the quality of data being collected in the LSST. Initial Zemax models proved this hypothesis to be correct, but it is important to weigh the improvements made versus the effort, risk, and cost especially when considering any hardware modifications to an instrument that is already running and collecting immense amounts of data each night. This paper investigates the impacts of installing an L3 baffle via a collection of mechanically focused studies, where the principal areas of focus are installation feasibility, baffle geometry, materials & coating selection, and potential impacts to the purge system.

AI.tldr: The paper discusses the commissioning of the Vera C. Rubin Observatory and the development of tools to mitigate stray light effects impacting data quality, particularly through a proposed baffle modification near the L3 lens of the LSSTCam.
AI.motivation: To address significant stray light effects that could impact data quality in the Rubin Observatory during its commissioning phase.
AI.method: Development of a comprehensive Zemax model to trace stray light paths and analysis of installation feasibility, baffle geometry, materials, and impact on the purge system regarding the proposed L3 baffle.
AI.result: Initial models validated the effectiveness of a baffle installation, indicating that it could enhance data quality from the LSSTCam by reducing stray light artifacts.
AI.conclusion: The paper evaluates the potential benefits of the L3 baffle installation against the costs, risks, and logistical challenges associated with modifying existing instrumentation.

title: Landau-Zener formula and resonant axion conversion in neutron star magnetospheres
summary: We investigate the Landau-Zener description of resonant axion-photon conversion in neutron star magnetospheres. We find that this picture often fails for axion conversions to millimeter-to-optical band photons due to the characteristic resonance width exceeding the size of the conversion region. This comparison of scales yields a simple criterion for evaluating the validity of the Landau-Zener formula. We verify this criterion numerically, and show that when invalid, the Landau-Zener conversion probability may significantly deviate from the numerical result. In light of these findings, we revise constraints on axions from neutron star optical-band polarization searches.

AI.tldr: This paper critiques the Landau-Zener model for axion-photon conversion in neutron star magnetospheres, highlighting its limitations in certain conditions and presenting revised constraints on axions based on these findings.
AI.motivation: To evaluate the validity of the Landau-Zener description in the context of axion-photon conversion and its implications for astrophysical observations.
AI.method: Analytical comparison of the resonance width and conversion region size, followed by numerical verification of the proposed criterion.
AI.result: Establishment of a criterion indicating when the Landau-Zener formula is valid or not, showing deviations in conversion probability under invalid conditions.
AI.conclusion: Revised constraints on axion presence based on new insights into photon polarization in neutron star magnetospheres.

title: Generalised Probabilistic Theories
summary: We give an introduction to research associated with the generalised probabilistic theories framework, also known as the convex framework. States are real vectors representing lists of probabilities of measurement outcomes. Convex combinations of the vectors represent probabilistic combinations of different state preparations. Transformations are real matrices. Measurement outcomes are represented by functionals of the states, inner products of the state with a real vector, whose values are the probability of the measurement outcome in question. The framework generalises quantum theory. We describe the operational meaning of the framework, and how the concepts can be defined in terms of cones of states and measurement outcome vectors. We describe how the classical and quantum probability theories are represented in the framework. We describe Bell non-locality and the theory with super-quantum non-locality known as box world. We discuss generalised Hamiltonian mechanics in the discrete case and in continuous phase space, including the role of negativity of the phase space density in contextuality and tunnelling.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces generalized probabilistic theories, detailing their operational meaning, representation of states and transformations, and their relation to classical and quantum theories, including discussions on Bell non-locality and Hamiltonian mechanics.
AI.motivation: To explore a broader framework that goes beyond conventional quantum theories and offers insights into foundational aspects of measurement and transformation in probabilistic theories.
AI.method: The framework is defined using vectors for states as probabilities, matrices for transformations, and functionals for measurement outcomes, along with concepts of cones in state representation.
AI.result: The paper illustrates how traditional classical and quantum probability fit into this generalized framework and discusses implications for Bell non-locality, including a super-quantum variant known as box world.
AI.conclusion: The generalized probabilistic theories framework provides a versatile foundation for understanding various probabilistic models, emphasizing the role of contextuality and phase space in theoretical physics.

title: Radiation-pressure instability is an artifact of constant-$α$ closure
comment: 4 pages + appendix (4 pages), 2 figures, A&A Letters
summary: The standard $α$-disk formalism parametrizes turbulent angular momentum transport through a dimensionless coefficient $α$, assumed to be spatially and thermodynamically invariant. While analytically convenient, this assumption leads to the well-known thermal and viscous instabilities in radiation-pressure dominated (RPD) regions. We show that this instability is not the consequence of radiation pressure, but is due to enforcing a constant $α$ across distinct thermodynamic regimes. Requiring the steady thin-disk (TD) to remain thermally stable and single-valued in the $\dot{M}$--$Σ$ plane yields a necessary condition on the stress response, expressed as $η_{\rm x} \equiv d\lnα_{\rm x}\,/\,d\ln X > 4/7$, where $X \equiv P_{\rm gas}/P_{\rm rad}$. The resulting viscosity law $α_{\rm x} \equiv α(X)$ emerges directly from the internal consistency of TD equations, without modifying the stress law or invoking any additional physics. $α_{\rm x}$ removes the RPD unstable branch. The disk structure becomes smooth and globally single-valued, with higher $Σ$ and $τ$ in the inner RPD disk, while preserving the standard effective-temperature profile. This increases thermal and inflow timescales, offering a natural route to accretion-state dependent variability without large-amplitude radiation-pressure limit cycles. It also motivates revisiting AGN disk tensions, including microlensing sizes and continuum reverberation lags with improved radiative-transfer modeling. The results show that the RPD instability, and possibly some associated AGN disk tensions, reflect an inconsistent viscosity closure.

AI.tldr: The study critiques the standard $α$-disk model in turbulence, showing its constant $α$ assumption leads to instability in radiation-pressure dominated regions. A new viscosity law, $α(X)$, is proposed to maintain stability without additional physics, improving the disk structure and potentially explaining AGN disk behaviors.
AI.motivation: To address the thermal and viscous instabilities in $α$-disk models due to the assumption of spatially invariant $α$ and to improve the modeling of accretion disks in astrophysics.
AI.method: Introduction of a new viscosity law $α_{m x}$ dependent on the gas-to-radiation pressure ratio $X$, derived from the internal consistency of the steady thin-disk equations.
AI.result: The new viscosity law $α_{m x}$ stabilizes the disk structure by eliminating the unstable branch and maintaining a consistent effective-temperature profile, leading to smoother disk properties and longer thermal timescales.
AI.conclusion: The RPD instability and related AGN disk tensions indicate that the traditional constant $α$ approach is inconsistent; the findings call for a reevaluation of accretion disk modeling using the new viscosity relation.

title: Investigation and Mitigation of a Prominent Off-Axis Stray Light Path in Rubin Observatory Commissioning
summary: The "scratched tape" stray light feature is the most prominent and prevalent stray light artifact identified during the commissioning of the Vera C. Rubin Observatory. The scratched tape feature originates when light from large off-axis angles (~20 deg) passes between the mid-level and center-section light baffles, reflects off the primary mirror, and illuminates the LSST Camera focal plane. This scenario represented an unobstructed stray light path to the sky during Rubin commissioning due to delays in the integration of the dome slit light-wind screen. This document describes the identification, modeling, characterization, and mitigation of the scratched tape stray light artifact.

AI.tldr: The paper discusses the identification and solutions for the 'scratched tape' stray light artifact in the Vera C. Rubin Observatory, caused by off-axis light paths during commissioning phases.
AI.motivation: To address the impact of stray light on the performance of the LSST Camera and overall observatory functionality.
AI.method: The paper describes the identification, modeling, characterization, and strategies for mitigating the scratched tape stray light artifact.
AI.result: The study successfully characterized the stray light path and proposed mitigation techniques to reduce its impact on observation quality.
AI.conclusion: Effective strategies for managing the scratched tape stray light artifact were developed, ultimately improving the observatory's operational performance.

title: Local Minimum of Spin-Sector Magic at the CP-Conserving Point in Low-Energy Neutron-Proton Scattering
summary: We study Magic generation in elastic neutron-proton scattering within a leading low-energy spin-sector ansatz that retains the one-pion-exchange spin structures and treats each scattering direction as a conditional two-qubit spin map. We show that the direction-averaged Magic is locally minimized at the CP-conserving (CPC) point $\barθ=0$ at the Clifford point $f_{\rm CPC}=π/4$, and for the representative non-Clifford CPC backgrounds analyzed here. At $f_{\rm CPC}=π/4$, the CPC spin map reduces to SWAP up to a phase and therefore generates zero Magic from stabilizer inputs. We further evaluate the complete spin-sector Magic functional by averaging over all 60 two-qubit stabilizer inputs and over scattering directions, and find that the curvature at $\barθ=0$ is positive only within specific windows of the effective CPC phase $f_{\rm CPC}$. These results identify the CPC point as a local Magic minimum within the restricted low-energy spin sector considered here.

AI.tldr: The study analyzes Magic generation in elastic neutron-proton scattering, identifying a local minimum at the CP-conserving point with specific conditions on the phase, while highlighting the role of one-pion-exchange spin structures.
AI.motivation: To explore the dynamics of Magic generation in neutron-proton scattering using spin maps, enhancing understanding in low-energy quantum interactions.
AI.method: The authors employ a leading low-energy ansatz treating scattering directions as conditional two-qubit spin maps, focusing on one-pion-exchange structures and averaging results over inputs and directions.
AI.result: Magic generation is locally minimized at the CP-conserving point and specific phase conditions, with findings indicating the curvature is only positive within certain effective CPC phase windows.
AI.conclusion: The findings establish the CP-conserving point as a local minimum for Magic in the analyzed spin sector, providing insights into the dynamics of quantum interactions under specific conditions.

title: Nonclassicality of a delayed remote-controlled quantum computing model
summary: Delegated quantum computing is likely to become the primary means for most people to access quantum computers in the future. However, these hardware inevitably operate beyond clients' control, raising concerns about potentially untrusted servers. A fundamental question thus arises -- how can clients verify that the server is genuinely performing quantum computations? Here, we demonstrate that a class of remote-controlled quantum computing (RCQC) models presents the nonclassical behavior verified in a semi-device-independent way. To achieve this, with slight modifications, these models can be described by the prepare-and-measure scenario. By verifying the violations of dimension witnesses, classical causal models can be ruled out, thereby showing nonclassicality of the RCQC model. Remarkably, in the prepare-and-measure scenario, this class of RCQC models happens to exhibit reversed temporal order in quantum information processing. We also explicitly confirm the nonclassical behaviors of a specific 1-U-M RCQC model belonging to this class as an example. This work bridges the fundamental quantum theory with the practical task of quantum computing.

AI.tldr: The paper explores remote-controlled quantum computing (RCQC) models, ensuring their nonclassicality through semi-device-independent verification, even in untrusted environments.
AI.motivation: To address the challenges of trust in quantum computing when clients access potentially untrusted servers, ensuring clients can verify computations.
AI.method: The study adapts RCQC models to a prepare-and-measure scenario, using dimension witnesses to confirm violations of classical causal models and demonstrate nonclassical behavior.
AI.result: The research shows that specific RCQC models exhibit nonclassical characteristics and instances of reversed temporal order in quantum information processing.
AI.conclusion: This work links theoretical aspects of quantum mechanics with practical quantum computing applications, enhancing trust in delegated quantum computing.

title: An overview of stray light findings and interpretation during on-sky commissioning of LSSTCam
summary: Wide-field telescopes are intrinsically difficult to shield from unwanted stray and scattered light, while the search to identify sources of contaminating light is frequently a challenging task. The Vera C.~Rubin Observatory, which achieved its first photon with the LSST Camera (LSSTCam) on April 15, 2025, will initiate a revolutionary era for the study of dark matter, dark energy, the transient sky, the Solar System, and the Milky Way. LSSTCam will provide near seeing-limited images of the sky in six bands ($u,g,r,i,z,y$) over a $3.^\circ 5$-diameter field of view, and over the course of a decade, it will execute the Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST). This work provides an overview of the dedicated stray and scattered light test campaign that has been undertaken since the start of Rubin commissioning. In particular, we highlight the processes used to characterize, model, and mitigate stray light present in LSSTCam images. The Rubin commissioning team created a series of testing and analysis tools to track stray light artifacts from their initial discovery through reproduction with timely observations, simulation using ray tracing to identify opto-mechanical origins, and finally devising corrective actions. The complex stray light features encountered by Rubin provide a wealth of experience for the future wide-field and extremely wide-field observatories. This work covers the many stages of a long journey that started with conceiving an innovative and challenging optical design, followed by the engineering and system engineering efforts to build it, to finally delivering an optimized and revolutionary cutting-edge facility.

AI.tldr: The paper discusses stray and scattered light challenges in wide-field telescopes, focusing on LSSTCam's development and testing processes to mitigate such issues, providing valuable insights for future observatories.
AI.motivation: To address the inherent difficulties in shielding wide-field telescopes from stray light, which complicates astronomical observations.
AI.method: A comprehensive testing campaign was initiated, utilizing tools for tracking stray light artifacts, ray tracing simulations for opto-mechanical origin identification, and corrective measures.
AI.result: The study documents the characterization and mitigation strategies for stray light in LSSTCam images, contributing extensive knowledge for future wide-field observatories.
AI.conclusion: The experiences gained in managing stray light during LSSTCam development will greatly benefit future observatories, enhancing their observational capabilities.

title: Nonlinear growth and amplification of phase-transition gravitational waves induced by cosmic expansion
summary: We perform the first three-dimensional hydrodynamical simulations of cosmological first-order phase transitions in an expanding background. These simulations consistently incorporate the effects of the evolving phase transition strength throughout the full nucleation process of slow phase transitions. We find that, in addition to reducing mean bubble separations via an effectively enhanced nucleation rate, cosmic expansion unexpectedly induces highly nonlinear growth in the gravitational wave energy fraction, ultimately leading to a significant $\mathcal{O}(10)$ to $\mathcal{O}(100)$ amplification of the gravitational wave spectra. This amplification is more pronounced for initially weak transitions than for those of initially intermediate strength. Our results highlight the challenge and importance of accurately modelling slow phase transitions while accounting for cosmic expansion.

AI.tldr: This study presents the first 3D simulations of cosmological first-order phase transitions, revealing that cosmic expansion enhances bubble nucleation and amplifies gravitational wave spectra significantly, especially for weak transitions.
AI.motivation: To investigate the impact of cosmic expansion on the process of slow first-order phase transitions and their associated gravitational wave signatures.
AI.method: Three-dimensional hydrodynamical simulations were performed, incorporating the evolving phase transition strength during the nucleation process in an expanding universe.
AI.result: Cosmic expansion increases nucleation rates and causes nonlinear growth in the gravitational wave energy fraction, amplifying the gravitational wave spectra by factors of 10 to 100, particularly for weak transitions.
AI.conclusion: Accurate modeling of slow phase transitions must consider cosmic expansion effects, as it significantly influences the gravitational wave signals generated.

title: Floquet Quasienergy-Resolved Dissipation, Dynamics, and Spectroscopy in Ultrastrong Cavity-QED
summary: Strong periodic driving of cavity-quantum electrodynamics (QED) in the ultrastrong-coupling regime creates nonequilibrium states whose dissipation is governed by Floquet quasienergies rather than undriven dressed resonances. However, modeling such a regime is a significant theoretical challenge, including a number of subtle problems such as the need to ensure gauge invariance for truncated matter-cavity systems with time-dependent driving. To fill this theoretical gap, we introduce a nonsecular Floquet generalized master equation framework for strongly driven open cavity-QED systems, formulated in the dressed basis of the quantum Rabi model and applicable to structured reservoirs without rotating-wave approximations. Our theory can thus model Floquet-driven dynamics in open ultrastrong-coupling cavity-QED, and demonstrates a wide range of quantum state control. Using strong optical pumping and parametric mechanical modulation, we compute long-time populations, fluorescence spectra, and the Floquet-Liouville eigenspectra, resolving observable resonances into hybridized quasienergy channels and decay rates. By systematically comparing with conventional time-independent dressed-basis generalized master equations, we show that static approaches only reproduce steady-state populations in restricted excitation regimes, and fail for frequency-resolved observables and break down under appropriate Floquet engineering, surprisingly, even for spectrally flat baths. Structured environments, such as Lorentzian-Ohmic reservoirs, further amplify these discrepancies through sideband-selective decay. Our results demonstrate that dissipation in driven ultrastrong cavity-QED is intrinsically quasienergy resolved and we establish Floquet-dissipative theory as an accurate and powerful framework for predicting spectra, controlling decay pathways, and engineering nonequilibrium quantum states and reservoirs.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a nonsecular Floquet generalized master equation framework to model nonequilibrium states in ultrastrong-coupling cavity-QED systems, addressing challenges in gauge invariance and spectral predictions.
AI.motivation: To address the theoretical complexities in modeling nonequilibrium states in cavity-QED under strong periodic driving, particularly the need for gauge invariance and accurate predictions of observables.
AI.method: Introduces a nonsecular Floquet generalized master equation in the dressed basis of the quantum Rabi model, applicable to structured reservoirs without rotating-wave approximations.
AI.result: The framework models Floquet-driven dynamics effectively, revealing discrepancies with conventional static approaches and demonstrating control over quantum states, observable resonances, and decay rates in open cavity-QED systems.
AI.conclusion: The study establishes Floquet-dissipative theory as a robust method for predicting and controlling the behavior of nonequilibrium quantum states and interactions under ultrastrong coupling.

title: The filter exchange system of the LSSTCam at the Vera C. Rubin Observatory
comment: 14 pages, 5 figures, proceeding of the SPIE conference
summary: The Filter Exchange System of the LSSTCam at the Vera C. Rubin Observatory is a critical subsystem enabling the Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) by performing rapid, repeatable exchanges among five large-format filters within a highly constrained in-camera volume. Since the start of on-sky operations in April 2025, the FES has routinely performed up to 40 filter exchanges per night, completing each change in under 90 seconds with a positioning repeatability of 100 micrometers in the focal plane. Safety and reliability are ensured through a dedicated software architecture. Drawing on over a year of operational experience, we report on the in-situ performance of this sophisticated system within the observatory environment, characterize the key performance metrics, and discuss how specific design choices have influenced system behavior and reliability in practice.

AI.tldr: The LSSTCam's Filter Exchange System enables quick filter swaps crucial for the Legacy Survey of Space and Time, operating with high efficiency and reliability.
AI.motivation: To support the LSST, a key goal of the Vera C. Rubin Observatory, by facilitating rapid and accurate filter exchanges.
AI.method: Operational data from over a year was analyzed to assess the system's performance and reliability metrics, emphasizing design impacts.
AI.result: The system conducts up to 40 exchanges per night in under 90 seconds with 100-micrometer repeatability, confirming efficient operation and reliability.
AI.conclusion: The analysis demonstrates the effectiveness of the Filter Exchange System, highlighting the role of design decisions in achieving operational success.

title: Optimization of perturbation series in QCD for physical quantities using the renormalization group: necessary conditions and partial results
summary: We explore approaches to numerically optimize a segment of the perturbative series for physical quantities using the QCD renormalization group. We apply these methods to the perturbative series for the coefficient function $C_{Bjps}$ of the Bjorken polarized sum rule and the Adler function $D_A$. Using various techniques proposed in the literature, we discuss the consequences of ``optimization.''

AI.tldr: The paper focuses on optimizing segments of the perturbative series for QCD quantities, specifically applying this to the Bjorken polarized sum rule and Adler function.
AI.motivation: The aim is to improve the numerical reliability of perturbative series in quantum chromodynamics (QCD) calculations.
AI.method: The authors utilize various numerical optimization techniques to enhance segments of the QCD perturbative series for specific physical quantities.
AI.result: The application of optimization methods to the coefficient function $C_{Bjps}$ and Adler function $D_A$ shows potential improvements in accuracy and convergence of the series.
AI.conclusion: The study highlights the importance of optimization in QCD perturbative series and its impact on theoretical predictions.

title: Energetics of non-Gaussianity in single mode cavities
summary: Non-Gaussian states play a central role in quantum technologies, making the ability to quantify non-Gaussianity essential. We introduce an energetic framework to characterize non-Gaussianity in single-mode bosonic states by decomposing the total energy into Gaussian and non-Gaussian contributions. For pure states, we show that the non-Gaussian component defines a valid measure of non-Gaussianity and establish its connection to the relative entropy of non-Gaussianity. As an illustration, we compare this measure with Wigner negativity and find that both are maximized in closely related parameter regimes. For mixed states, we demonstrate that the non-Gaussian contribution acts as a faithful witness of non-Gaussianity. Our results reveal an energetic fine structure underlying non-Gaussianity and may provide practical insights for the efficient generation of non-Gaussian states.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a novel energetic framework to quantify non-Gaussianity in single-mode bosonic states by separating total energy into Gaussian and non-Gaussian parts, establishing relevant measures and connections to entropy.
AI.motivation: Characterizing non-Gaussianity is crucial for advancements in quantum technologies.
AI.method: An energetic framework is used to decompose energy contributions in single-mode bosonic states, defining non-Gaussianity measures for both pure and mixed states.
AI.result: The non-Gaussian measure exhibits a relationship with the relative entropy of non-Gaussianity, with connections to Wigner negativity observed in parameter regimes.
AI.conclusion: The findings highlight an intricate structure of non-Gaussianity that may facilitate efficient non-Gaussian state generation.

title: Hadronic exceptional points
summary: Exceptional points, where eigenvalues and eigenvectors coalesce, are a defining feature of non-Hermitian systems and have been extensively observed in photonic, atomic, and condensed matter systems. However, they have received little attention in quantum chromodynamics (QCD), which is the fundamental theory of quarks, gluons, and hadrons. We propose that imaginary magnetic fields provide a simple realization of non-Hermitian dynamics in hadronic systems. Based on two theoretical approaches, a hadronic effective Lagrangian and a constituent quark model, we compute mass spectra of neutral mesons and find exceptional points separating the real-spectrum and complex-eigenvalue regimes. In small fields, the real spectrum exhibits level attraction between hadronic states, whereas in larger fields, hadrons are deconfined, which is a signature of a field-induced inverted potential. Our findings open a new avenue for studying QCD dynamics in non-Hermitian environments.

AI.tldr: This study introduces imaginary magnetic fields as a means to explore non-Hermitian dynamics in quantum chromodynamics (QCD), revealing exceptional points that differentiate between real and complex spectrums of meson masses.
AI.motivation: The research aims to fill the gap in investigating exceptional points in QCD, which have been overlooked despite their significant implications in other physical systems.
AI.method: Using a hadronic effective Lagrangian and a constituent quark model, the researchers compute the mass spectra of neutral mesons under imaginary magnetic fields and identify exceptional points.
AI.result: The study finds that small imaginary magnetic fields lead to level attraction among hadronic states, while larger fields result in deconfinement of hadrons, indicating a field-induced inverted potential.
AI.conclusion: These findings suggest a novel approach to studying QCD dynamics, particularly in non-Hermitian contexts, potentially influencing the understanding of hadronic physics.

title: Topological phase transition in chaotic optomechanical systems
summary: Hidden structures with well-defined predictability are uncovered in the evolution of a chaotic optomechanical system from the perspective of the $ε$-machine. Tuning the frequency of the driving laser can switch off this predictability, and such behaviour corresponds to a phase transition that is deeply related to topological changes in phase space. The transition probabilities between causal states allow us to define an entropy (uncertainty) that serves as an effective order parameter. This phase transition can be readily demonstrated in currently available experiments by monitoring the quadrature of the optical mode. We hope that this work could fundamentally broaden the regimes of cavity micromechanics and nonlinear optics.

AI.tldr: This paper reveals predictable structures in a chaotic optomechanical system and examines their behavior under external frequency tuning, identifying a phase transition tied to phase space topology.
AI.motivation: To explore the predictability of chaotic systems and their phase transitions through the lens of $ε$-machines.
AI.method: Analyzing the transition probabilities between causal states to establish an entropy that acts as an order parameter, and linking these findings to experimental observables in optomechanics.
AI.result: Identification of a phase transition affected by laser frequency tuning, demonstrating changes in predictability and entropy that relate to topological alterations in phase space.
AI.conclusion: The research offers new insights that could expand the applications of cavity micromechanics and nonlinear optics.

title: Energy-Flow Moments for Elliptic Gluon Wigner Tomography
summary: The elliptic small-$x$ gluon Wigner distribution correlates transverse momentum with impact parameter, but it is usually accessed through exclusive diffractive dijets whose recoil is sensitive to soft radiation. We propose instead an azimuthal energy-flow moment in DIS dijet production. Within leading-power small-$x$ dijet factorization, its normalized $\cos2φ$ moment is a linear projection of the elliptic Wigner harmonic after a calculable kinematic subtraction, while the final-state energy weighting is infrared and collinear safe. In conjugate recoil space a rotationally scalar Sudakov factor evolves the isotropic and elliptic channels through a fixed $J_0/J_2$ Hankel pair without $W_0\to W_1$ leakage. A proof-of-principle calculation gives a per-mille Sudakov-level moment in an unoptimized conservative window, while auxiliary perturbative-window scans reach several per mille. The observable therefore formulates elliptic Wigner tomography as a moment-level energy-flow measurement whose statistical reach can be assessed by simple angular-moment counting.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes an azimuthal energy-flow moment for analyzing small-$x$ gluon dynamics in DIS dijet production, bypassing conventional methods and offering a new way to measure elliptic Wigner distributions.
AI.motivation: To improve the analysis of the elliptic small-$x$ gluon Wigner distribution, which is typically accessed via methods sensitive to soft radiation.
AI.method: An azimuthal energy-flow moment is introduced, derived from leading-power small-$x$ dijet factorization and defined as the normalized $	ext{cos}2φ$ moment, with a calculable kinematic subtraction ensuring infrared and collinear safety.
AI.result: A per-mille Sudakov-level moment is obtained, with auxiliary scans indicating potential for higher precision in measuring the elliptic Wigner distribution.
AI.conclusion: The proposed observable offers a novel framework for elliptic Wigner tomography, allowing for effective statistical reach through angular-moment counting.

title: Entanglement Structure Across $\mathbb{Z}_n$ Phase Transitions in 1D Rydberg Atom Arrays
summary: Multipartite quantum entanglement plays a crucial role in the emergence of different quantum phases and their transitions in quantum many-body systems. It is of general interest to know what sort of analysis on quantum entanglement can bring us a profound insight to understand the rich dynamics of quantum many-body systems. In this work we study the characteristics of quantum entanglement in relation to $\mathbb{Z}_n$-ordered phases emerging under a varied strength of 1-dim Rydberg interaction. We propose an approach based on the structure of pair-wise entanglement across the Rydberg chain using two-qubit concurrence as an entanglement measure. We define an entanglement-structure factor via Fourier analysis of total concurrence at each site and address $\mathbb{Z}_n$ phase transitions in comparison with the conventional order-parameter based on local density, i.e. magnetization. We also discuss how the required two-qubit concurrence can be measured in analog Rydberg atom arrays using site-selective erasure and parametrized laser pulses. Our investigation suggests that an entanglement-structure-based approach can provide a powerful tool in analyzing symmetry-breaking in quantum phase transitions.

AI.tldr: The study explores multipartite quantum entanglement's role in quantum phase transitions, focusing on $	extbackslashmathbb{Z}_n$-ordered phases influenced by Rydberg interactions. It introduces a framework employing two-qubit concurrence for analyzing entanglement, proposing a novel entanglement-structure factor, and comparing it with conventional order parameters. Measurement techniques using laser pulses are also discussed, highlighting the potential of this approach in studying symmetry-breaking during phase transitions.
AI.motivation: To understand the dynamics of quantum many-body systems better through entanglement analysis, particularly in relation to $	extbackslashmathbb{Z}_n$-ordered phases and Rydberg interactions.
AI.method: The methodology involves analyzing pair-wise entanglement using two-qubit concurrence and defining an entanglement-structure factor through Fourier analysis of total concurrence. The study compares these findings to traditional order-parameter approaches, such as magnetization.
AI.result: The investigation provides insights into $	extbackslashmathbb{Z}_n$ phase transitions by employing an entanglement-structure-based approach, suggesting its effectiveness in revealing symmetry-breaking phenomena.
AI.conclusion: The approach outlined may serve as a powerful analytic tool for examining quantum phase transitions and understanding the role of entanglement in quantum many-body systems.

title: Collinearly Improved Balitsky-Kovchegov Evolution of the Gluon Wigner Distribution
summary: We study how collinearly improved small-$x$ evolution modifies the elliptic gluon Wigner distribution and its coherent diffractive dijet $\cos2φ$ signal. Starting from the $SO(3)$-symmetric Gubser initial condition, we compare fixed-coupling leading-order (LO) BK evolution with the Iancu--Madrigal--Mueller--Soyez--Triantafyllopoulos (IMST) collinearly improved BK prescription, project the evolved dipole to Wigner/GTMD harmonics, and fold the result with photon wave-function hard factors. Within the $SO(3)$-projected framework, the resummed evolution moves the elliptic node and changes the rapidity and hard-scale dependence of $C_2^{\rm coh}=\langle\cos2φ\rangle$, rather than acting as a simple normalization shift. The effect is largest in node-sensitive windows but remains visible in broader sign-stable bins. Direct daughter-coordinate RHS tests and direct $(r,b,φ)$ evolution quantify the residual projection ambiguity and check the observed trend. Projection-level EIC-like finite-bin estimates show that balanced high-$Δ$ candidate bins offer a better compromise between elliptic signal and denominator weight than the narrow bins with the largest ratio.
